analysis.title: UBS TECH DAILY CURT COMMENT: BESI, Tieto, ASML - whats priced in, DDOG
key_insights: About $250bn of AI-related capital raise announcements have come recently, including SpaceX, about $95bn for Meta per Bloomberg, and a new AVGO-backed LLM financing vehicle.
The AVGO financing is a $63B structure for shipments in C2027. AVGO provides residual value support of about 72.5% of the amount, and its exposure declines as lease payments are made.
AMAT is buying more of BESI. The author notes that 20% is a proper blocking stake.

AMAT's release last night says it has no intention to increase its Besi investment beyond about 20% and does not intend to seek board representation. The April 14, 2025 AMAT release said it had no plans to buy additional Besi shares, so the two statements are being compared.

Tieto cut its FY organic outlook to (5)-(6)% from (3)-(5)%, citing soft demand and internal transformation efforts in Consulting. Software volumes were also weak in Financial Services and Industry. The author sees little read-across to UBS's covered names.
Tieto Q3 organic growth was -11%, which implies (3)-1% in Q4. H1 was -4%. Tieto raised margin guidance to 15.5-16.0% from 14.8-15.8%, which the author attributes to a likely reduced bonus pool.

UBS's framework shows wide dispersion in what is priced in for AI. ASML, STM and NXP are the most de-risked, with share prices implying cuts of more than 50% to UBS's 2028E AI EPS estimates. Nokia and Soitec are the most demanding, with valuations implying upgrades or only modest downgrades.

ASML: extrapolating its 2011-21 EPS CAGR to 2028E gives non-AI EPS of EUR40-45, against about EUR85 in buyside expectations. That implies roughly half of EPS is AI-related. Applying the historical 26x multiple to the non-AI base leaves only 11x for AI earnings, consistent with a roughly 50% haircut.

On EUR40-45 of non-AI EPS, ASML would trade at about 30-35x, against historical 1Y/2Y averages of about 31x/27x. UBS sees an asymmetry because the valuation reflects an AI correction that its compute work does not yet support.

UBS estimates each 1GW of AI compute represents EUR500-900m of lithography spend, or about 0.6-1% of ASML's 2028E revenue and 2% of EPS. The roughly 50% haircut to AI EPS equates to about 25GW removed from 2027/28E capacity expectations.
UBS forecasts about 50GW of industry additions in 2027E and 60-70GW in 2028E. The implied 25GW cut is therefore about 20% downside to AI compute demand across 2027/28E.

The buyside bogey for ASML FY28E EPS is about EUR85 per share, against EUR78 on the sell side. UBS estimates EUR85 can be supported by roughly 115-120 EUV shipments and $250-275bn of WFE in 2028E, meaningfully below the often-discussed >$300bn WFE scenario.

sector_views.rationale: The author sees significant dispersion in what is priced in for AI. ASML, STM and NXP are most de-risked, while Nokia and Soitec are most demanding.

earnings_insights: Tieto FY organic outlook lowered to (5)-(6)% from (3)-(5)%, company guidance. Q3 organic growth was -11%, which implies (3)-1% in Q4. H1 was -4%.
Tieto margin guidance raised to 15.5-16.0% from 14.8-15.8%, company guidance. The author assumes a reduced bonus pool.
ASML FY28E EPS: buyside expectation about EUR85, sell side EUR78 (estimates, not reported).
risk_factors: Heavy equity and debt issuance tied to AI (about $250bn recently) is a supply and funding risk for semis.
If AI compute demand falls more than the roughly 20% already implied in ASML's valuation, ASML EPS faces further downside.
Nokia and Soitec valuations still imply upgrades or only modest downgrades, so they are exposed if AI expectations reset.

tension_points.bull_case: The valuation already implies a roughly 50% haircut to AI EPS, equal to about 25GW of capacity removed. UBS's compute work does not yet support such a correction, so it sees asymmetry to the upside.
tension_points.bear_case: If AI compute demand falls by more than the roughly 20% implied, EPS and the multiple face further downside. Non-AI EPS of EUR40-45 would still put ASML at 30-35x.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI compute additions falling well below UBS's forecast of about 50GW in 2027E and 60-70GW in 2028E.

theme_stances.key_argument: The market is already discounting a material AI reset in ASML that UBS's compute work does not yet support.
theme_stances.evidence: valuation reflects a meaningful AI correction that our compute work does not yet support
